clue.text: Spooner's had no alcohol for a meal

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the phrase meant here must have its initial sounds exchanged

parts.note: to have no alcohol is to lack punch, the mixed party drink; swapping the L and P sounds gives the phrase in the grid

explanation.surface: Someone apparently reports that Spooner went teetotal for a dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first sounds of LACKED PUNCH and you get PACKED LUNCH. Punch is the fruity alcoholic bowl drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed lunch is food boxed up at home and eaten midday, so it is a kind of meal.

clue.text: Recalling medic for mission

parts.note: à la means in the style of, i.e. recalling or reminiscent of
MO is a Medical Officer

explanation.surface: A doctor being called back from an overseas posting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalling' looks like a reversal signal; it is the French-derived À LA, meaning 'in the manner of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo in San Antonio, Texas, was originally a Spanish Catholic mission before the famous 1836 siege.

clue.text: Odd characters in Kansas really being wicked

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, are the ones to keep from the state's name

parts.note: letters 1, 3 and 5 of the state name
really and very are both intensifiers

explanation.surface: Strange folk out in Kansas are said to be truly evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Knavery is roguish dishonest behaviour, the state or conduct of a rogue, so it is a noun for being wicked.

clue.text: Republican leaving drunk recited falsehood, say

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the remaining letters lurch into a new order
the party member walks out, so that letter goes from the word that follows

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for Republican
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tipsy politician walks out after reciting a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R from RECITED, then rearrange the six letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is one example of deceit, the practice of misleading people, hence the 'say' flagging an example.

clue.text: António Guterres nearly departs to get kind of fuel

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter of the title is cut off

parts.note: Guterres is Secretary-General, so he is the UN leader
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: The UN Secretary-General almost leaves to fill up with petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: António Guterres has been Secretary-General of the United Nations since 2017.
explanation.definitionFit: Unleaded petrol is motor fuel without added lead compounds, the standard grade sold at modern pumps.

clue.text: Program incorporating a German number

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take something into the body, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a computer program is code
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: Some software that includes a German numeral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as numb-er, something that deadens pain, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is an opiate painkiller, so it is something that numbs; that is the crossword trick reading of number.

clue.text: Tree sprouting bananas in lobby, perhaps

indicators.note: to go bananas is to go crazy, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: all thirteen letters are used

explanation.surface: A tree growing bananas in a hotel foyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lobby' looks like an entrance hall to go with the picture; it is the political lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobby is a group campaigning to influence lawmakers, one example of an interest group, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Peach yogurt occasionally, following roast

indicators.note: following places the sampled letters after the word for roast

parts.note: to roast and to knock both mean to criticise harshly

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter of the dairy product is kept

parts.note: letters 2, 4 and 6

explanation.surface: Peach yogurt now and again, after a roast dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peach' looks like the fruit flavour; it is the slang sense of a stunner.
explanation.definitionFit: A peach is informal for a very attractive person or thing, and a knockout is the same: a stunner.

clue.text: One taking off coat gently — isn't one taking off everything?

parts.note: p for piano, the musical direction to play softly
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't
someone who removes all their clothes

explanation.surface: A wry question: if a paint remover takes off a coat gently, isn't a performer who removes all clothing the same thing?
explanation.walkthrough: The 'coat' is a coat of paint, not clothing, though the second half leans on the clothing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint stripper is a chemical solvent that removes a coat of paint from a surface.

clue.text: African bounder in America, between cities there

indicators.note: between puts one item in the gap separating two others

parts.note: New York and Los Angeles are American cities, 'there' pointing back to America
A is a standard abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: An African cad living in the US, moving between its cities.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bounder' looks like an old word for a cad; here it is literally an animal that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa, and antelopes leap, so it is an African bounder.

clue.text: Overlooking loch, visited one area in Scotland

indicators.note: to overlook something is to miss it out, so that letter is skipped

parts.note: to visit someone is to call on them
Roman numeral one
A is a standard abbreviation for area
L is the map abbreviation for loch or lake

explanation.surface: A tourist with a view over a loch visits one part of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Ls goes from CALLED ON. 'area in Scotland' looks like the definition, but 'in' is a link and Scotland alone is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the Latin name the Romans gave northern Britain, still used poetically for Scotland.

clue.text: Wino coming in uncovered Ted Heath's secrets

indicators.note: the drinker enters, so it sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: Erica is the botanical genus of heath and heather
a sot is a habitual drunkard

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters of the name are removed

parts.note: the name without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A drunk barges in on the exposed secrets of former Prime Minister Ted Heath.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath looks like the 1970s British Prime Minister, but the two words are split up, and heath is read as the plant genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are obscure matters understood only by an inner circle, so this is knowledge kept from outsiders.

clue.text: Like some Native Americans jailed over there?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: relating to the Inca people of the Andes
second meaning, split as two words: locked up, in American slang where the can is prison

explanation.walkthrough: 'over there' means in America, where 'the can' is slang for jail, so the second reading is two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca empire ruled the Andes, so its peoples count among the indigenous peoples of the Americas.

clue.text: Still holding coat of lovely logger called John

indicators.note: holding means one word wraps around the other

parts.note: still and even both intensify a comparison: still better, even better

indicators.note: a coat is the outside layer, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A lumberjack named John still holding a lovely coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'logger' looks like a lumberjack; it is someone who keeps a log. John Evelyn was a 17th-century English diarist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Evelyn kept a famous diary of Restoration England, a daily record, so he was a keeper of a log.

clue.text: Sense some having a row must welcome agreement

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rowing eight is a boat crew of eight oarsmen
yes is the word of agreement

explanation.surface: People quarrelling should be glad to reach a settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having a row' suggests quarrelling; it means rowing a boat, as an eight does.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight, the faculty of vision, is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Dope, you heard, admitted to love for Liberal

parts.note: dope and gen are both slang for information

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside, so the sound-alike letter goes within the god of love

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by its sound, as a single letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the letter U sounds like the word you

explanation.surface: Information heard by you, revealed to a romantic partner, about a Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' with its capital looks like the political party; it is the everyday sense of open-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean lavish or free-giving, as in a liberal helping, which is the same as generous.

clue.text: Filling displays, fish shops may use these

indicators.note: something filling a space sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to bare is to expose or display
a common fish

explanation.surface: Fish shops put on displays of their fillings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish shops' reads as a single phrase in the surface; the split falls between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Bar codes are the striped machine-readable labels scanned at shop tills to identify products.

clue.text: 19 number of driving aids on the wagon

parts.note: in golf, a tee is the peg the ball rests on for a drive
19 is OVERALL, and the overall number is the total

explanation.surface: An overall count of teeing pegs on a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as a 'tee total', the total of tees. 'On the wagon' is idiom for not drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the wagon is to abstain from alcohol, which is exactly what a teetotal person does.

clue.text: General stops guerrilla revolutionaries after uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising is something going upwards, so the letters are read from bottom to top
a stop plugs a gap, so the answer sits across the join of two words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A general halts rebel fighters after an insurrection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer; it is the adjective meaning all-round.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall as an adjective means comprehensive or taken as a whole, the same as general in 'the general picture'.

clue.text: After religious celebration, old monarch's more livid

parts.note: Whit, or Whitsun, is the Christian festival of Pentecost
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: An old king grows angrier after a church feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'livid' suggests furious; it also means ashen, deathly pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid can mean pale or ashen, as in livid with shock, so more livid means paler, nearer to white.

clue.text: Riot guards tense, spelling trouble here?

indicators.note: a guard surrounds what it protects, so the following letters go inside

parts.note: a riot and a hoot are both something hilarious
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
sp. is the proofreader's mark for a spelling error

explanation.surface: Police at a riot are on edge, which bodes badly.
explanation.walkthrough: A riot here is a very funny thing, not civil disorder. The question mark signals that trouble merely tends to happen at a hotspot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspot is a place of conflict or unrest, so it is where trouble is likely to break out.

clue.text: Blundering when dropping grand cake

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so that letter falls out of the word

parts.note: to muff is to bungle
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone drops a fancy gâteau through clumsiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the G off the end of MUFFING.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffin is a small sweet baked cake, often made in a paper case.

clue.text: Hike from capital south, about to go outside

indicators.note: going outside means wrapping round the other letters

parts.note: re means about or concerning
A1 means first-rate, and capital is an old exclamation of approval meaning the same
S is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A walk south from the capital, roughly where you leave the city.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written AI. 'Hike' looks like a walk; it is a price or pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: A hike in pay or prices is an increase, and a pay rise in American English is a raise.

clue.text: Places for trying trendy suit

parts.note: law courts are where cases are tried
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: Where to try on a fashionable suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' looks like trying on clothes; it is trying a case. 'suit' is wooing, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay suit to someone is an old way of saying woo them, so suit and courtship both mean romantic pursuit.

clue.text: Fast runner on motorway getting some sultanas?

parts.note: the hare is a proverbially quick animal
M as in M1, the British motorway prefix

explanation.surface: A speedy runner on the motorway acquires some dried fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sultanas' looks like dried grapes; it means sultans' wives.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the group of wives of a sultan, and the wife of a sultan is a sultana.

clue.text: Novel found to contain a lot of compassion, which is novel

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so the shortened word goes within the rearranged one
novel means new, so the following word is given a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to have heart is to have compassion

explanation.surface: A new book is discovered to be full of kindness, something new in itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The two uses of 'novel' are the trick: first an indicator meaning new arrangement, then the definition, not a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Unheard-of means never known before, unprecedented, which is what something novel is.

clue.text: Faultless boxing succeeded, getting boxer's prize

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing as in a box, so one letter is put inside the other word

parts.note: pure means without fault
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A boxer wins a flawless fight and collects the prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' fits the surface's fight; it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse is the prize money for a boxing match, put up for the fighters.

clue.text: Criminal's head down before sentence, it's said behind bars

indicators.note: the head is at the top, so only the first letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the initial letter
to be down in a game is to be losing
doing time is serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A criminal hangs their head before sentencing, as is said in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind bars' looks like prison; it means behind a pub bar, where staff call last orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing time is the phrase a pub landlord calls out from behind the bar when it is time to stop serving drinks.
